interpretationBounds: At target 70 only, observed low utilization ratio is 0.50, consistent with target minus 20 percentage points. Other targets were not measured.
Use snapshot comparisons for observed identity/action preservation; do not infer a refresh from a successful SetAlarmState or PutScalingPolicy response alone.
The table-read manual state transition is synthetic. Untouched table-write and GSI alarm histories are natural controls.
Empty ScalingActivities responses are observations at their timestamps, not a guarantee that maintenance can never create activities.
Explicit policy calls can overlap ongoing native maintenance. Compare alarm creation/deletion history timestamps against each PutScalingPolicy before attributing replacement to that API.

supplementalCapture.reason: The live native run exposed natural consumed-low scale-in before provisioned-high maintenance. A synchronized supplementary aws_cli.observe capture reapplied capacity after the natural snapshot and before explicit PutScalingPolicy calls. Retired alarm histories were read after cleanup. The retained script incorporates these evidence-driven steps for future runs.
supplementalCapture.ordering: Calls are sorted by actual client startedAt timestamps, including concurrent read-only metric/history observations. Sequence numbers and snapshot references were remapped without changing native input/output.

observedRules.alarmFamily: Four alarms per read/write policy for table and GSI when DisableScaleIn=false: consumed high/low and provisioned high/low; sixteen total.
observedRules.consumedHigh: At target70: Sum, Period60, EvaluationPeriods2, GreaterThanThreshold, capacity*60*0.70.
observedRules.consumedLow: At target70: Sum, Period60, EvaluationPeriods15, LessThanThreshold, capacity*60*0.50. Consistent with a 20-percentage-point margin; other targets not measured.
observedRules.provisionedMaintenance: Average, Period300, EvaluationPeriods3, threshold=current capacity when the alarm family is created. High uses GreaterThanThreshold, low LessThanThreshold.
observedRules.syntheticDelivery: After real table-read capacity2->4, a manually delivered ProvisionedCapacityHigh action with fresh native-style recentDatapoints [4,4,4] succeeded. Four table-read alarms were deleted/replaced, thresholds84->168,60->120,2->4; policy action ARN including createdBy was preserved. Immediate post-delivery scaling-activity queries returned empty arrays including not-scaled activities.
observedRules.naturalObservation: Natural consumed-low alarms reported fifteen real zero datapoints and caused successful scale-in to table2/3 and GSI4/5. Failed activities reported AlreadyAtMinCapacity and TargetServicePutResourceAsUnscalable. Subsequently all four current ProvisionedCapacityHigh alarms naturally entered ALARM at16:37:14-16:37:57 UTC on three prior-capacity datapoints (16:21,16:26,16:31 UTC) and recorded successful action delivery. Before the second manual increase, thresholds/identities stayed unchanged because actual capacities already matched post-scale-in thresholds. All returned activity causes were consumed AlarmLow, not provisioned maintenance.
observedRules.explicitRefresh: Same-configuration PutScalingPolicy returned Success for all four dimensions after the second actual increase. Table-read returned and retained old alarm identities/capacity2 thresholds despite DescribeTable=4. GSI-read Put returned the old family; replacement appeared afterward. Table-write and GSI-write families had already been replaced automatically before their Put calls. These rows do not prove that PutScalingPolicy itself synchronously refreshes capacity thresholds; ongoing natural maintenance confounds causal attribution.
observedRules.publishedMetrics: Final GetMetricStatistics at Period60 and300 both returned three sparse provisioned bins at16:25,16:30,16:35 UTC, SampleCount1 each, values table4/5 and GSI6/7. No absent minute was converted to zero.
observedRules.cleanup: Policies, scalable targets, table/GSI and owned alarms were verified absent. Existing service-linked role was only read and never altered. Resource lifetime was about21.2 minutes.
observedRules.naturalThresholdRefresh: After the second actual capacity increase became ACTIVE at16:38:30 UTC, table-write and GSI-write replacement ProvisionedCapacityHigh alarms were created at16:38:37.631 and16:38:40.137 UTC, BEFORE their explicit PutScalingPolicy calls began at16:38:44.454 and16:38:45.959. Their entire four-alarm families had new names/ARNs, retained policy action IDs, and current-capacity thresholds. This is positive automatic maintenance evidence, independent of those explicit API calls. GSI-read replacement occurred at16:38:57.247 after its policy call; attribution is not isolated.

boundedUnknowns: Natural provisioned-high ALARM/action delivery is observed for all four dimensions, and automatic threshold replacement before explicit policy calls is observed for table-write/GSI-write. An unconfounded first-increase lifecycle without intervening idle consumed-low scale-in was not isolated.

A successful explicit PutScalingPolicy did not itself demonstrate synchronous capacity refresh: table-read retained old thresholds and GSI-read returned old identities. Eventual table-read refresh latency and the independent causal effect of PutScalingPolicy remain unknown.
Synthetic immediate activity arrays were empty; later activity rows all name consumed-low alarms. This does not guarantee that every maintenance action can never record an activity.
Threshold formula at target values other than70 and behavior at capacities above8 were not measured.
